---
title: "Install Positron Instructions"
---

Positron is Posit's data-science IDE (made by the same company that makes RStudio). It has R and Python support built in, a familiar RStudio-style layout (console, environment, plots, viewer), and works for Quarto documents.

If you already have RStudio working, you don't need Positron — they do the same job. Pick one.

## Step 1: Install R

Positron uses R that's installed on your machine, so install R first.

- Go to [https://cran.rstudio.com/](https://cran.rstudio.com/).
- At the top of the page, select the download for your operating system:
    - **macOS** — click the latest `R-x.y.z.pkg` installer. Download and run it.
    - **Windows** — click **base**, then **Download R for Windows**. Download and run the installer.

## Step 2: Install Positron

- Go to [https://positron.posit.co/](https://positron.posit.co/){target="_blank"} and click the download for your operating system.
- Download and run the installer.

When you open Positron, it should detect your R installation automatically. If it doesn't, open **Preferences** → search for "R" → set the interpreter path.

## Step 3: Try it

- **File → New File → R File.** Type `plot(1:10)` and press **Cmd/Ctrl + Enter**. A plot should appear in the Plots pane on the right.
- **File → New File → Quarto Document.** Use the **Render** button (top toolbar) to produce an HTML file.

## Notes

- Course examples and screenshots were written for RStudio. Positron's layout is close but not identical — pane names and menu items match about 90% of the time. If a step in a tutorial says "Plots pane," Positron has one too; if it says "Files pane," that's the Explorer on the left.
- Positron handles Quarto rendering without extra setup. You don't need to install the Quarto CLI separately.
